OBITUARY REFERENCE 
 MR. CHAIRMAN: Hon. Members, I refer with profound sorrow to the passing away of  
S h r i  M u n a v v a r  H a s a n ,  a  f o r m e r  M e m b e r  o f  t h i s  H o u s e  a n d  a  s i t t i n g  M e m b e r  o f  t h e  1 4 t h  L o k  
Sabha. 
 Shri Munavvar Hasan passed away on the 10th December, 2008 in a road accident at the 
age of 44 years. 
 Born at Kairana, in district Muzaffarnagar in  Uttar Pradesh in May, 1964, Shri Hasan had his 
education at Muzaffarnagar. 
 An agriculturist by vocation, Shri Hasan stea dfastly worked for the cause of social justice 
and for the welfare of the poor and deprived sections of the society. 
 The legislative career of Shri Hasan starte d with the membership of the Uttar Pradesh 
Legislative Assembly in 1991 and he served as Me mber of that Assembly for two terms from 1991 
to 1996. He was a Member of the Uttar Pradesh Legislative Council from January, 2004 to May, 
2004 and was also a Member of the 11th and 14th Lok Sabha. 
 Shri Munavvar Hasan represented the State of  Uttar Pradesh in this House from July, 1998 
to January, 2004. 
 In the passing away of Shri Munavvar Hasan, the country has lost an able Parliamentarian. 
 We deeply mourn the passing away of Shri Munavvar Hasan. 
 I request Members to rise in their places an d observe silence as a mark of respect to the 
memory of the departed. 
(Hon. Members then stood in silence for one minute) 
 MR. CHAIRMAN : Secretary-General will convey to the members of the bereaved family our 
sense of profound sorrow and deep sympathy.

WRITTEN ANSWERS TO STARRED AND UNSTARRED QUESTIONS 
3G spectrum bids 
 *141. SHRI VIJAY JAWAHARLAL DARDA: 
  SHRI GIREESH KUMAR SANGHI: 
 Will the Minister of COMMUNICATIONS AN D INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be pleased to 
state: 
 (a)  whether his Ministry has delayed 3G spectrum bids considerably; 
 (b) if so, whether the Ministry of Finance has also urged his Ministry to hold auction as 
early as possible so that the estimated Rs. 40,000 crores can be budgeted in the current fiscal 
books to bridge the fiscal deficit; 
 (c) if so, whether a number of political partie s have also criticised Government over the 
favouring of chosen corporates; 
 (d) if so, whether the new 3G telecom is to  share a 3 per cent revenue with Government; 
and 
 (e) if so, by what time a final decision in this regard is likely to be taken? 

 4 
 THE MINISTER OF COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY (SHRI A. RAJA) : (a) 
No, Sir. 
 (b) The Government has announced detailed guidelines for auction and allotment of 
spectrum for 3G telecom services on 1st August, 2008 and certain amendments on  
11st September, 2008. As per the guidelines, any person (i) who holds a UAS/CMTS licence: of 
(ii) (a) who has previous experience of running 3G telecom Services: and (b) gives an 
undertaking to obtain Unified Access Servic es Licence (UASL) as per Department of 
Telecommunications guidelines dated 14.12.2005 before starting telecom operations, can bid for 
3G spectrum. The Ministry of Finance has desired that the auction of 3G Spectrum be 
conducted by January, 2009 and the full amount deposited in the exchequer by February, 2009. 
The amount which would be realized from the auction shall e known only after the auction 
process is complete. 
 (c) No, Sir. 
 (d) and (e) The proposal to levy annual spectr um charges for stand alone 3G operators will 
be finalized shortly. 
Scheme for urban transport planning 
 *142. SHRI GIREESH KUMAR SANGHI: 
  DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY: 
 Will the Minister of URBAN DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 (a) whether Government is likely to launch a Rs. 152 crore scheme for urban transport 
planning to encourage states to upgrade public  transport systems which are crumbling in most 
cities including the Metros; 
 (b) if so, whether his Ministry’s programme that is aimed at promoting eco-friendly,  
safe, comfortable and affordable public transpor t would push cities to take up studies to  
prepare detailed project reports after comprehe nsive and thorough evaluation of alternate 
technologies; 
 (c)  if so, whether his Ministry has al ready started studies in this regard; and 
 (d) if so, by what time a final decision in this regard is likely to be taken? 
 THE MINISTER OF URBAN DEVELOPMENT (SHR I S. JAIPAL REDDY) : (a) to (d) A new 
centrally sponsored scheme of Urban Transport Planning has been launched by the Government 
from August, 2008 to provide central financial assi stance to States/Urban Local Bodies, (ULBs) 
upto 80% total cost for taking up various traffic and transportation studies etc. and upto 50% of 
the total cost for preparation of Detailed Proj ect Reports (DPRs). The estimated cost of the 
scheme during the Eleventh Fi ve Year Plan including State/Urban Local Bodies share is  
Rs. 124.70 crore. The Scheme covers a wide ga mut of urban transport planning matters for 
promoting comprehensive urban mobility plan integrating land-use and transport, preparation of 
Detailed Projects Reports (DPRs) , Clean Development Mechanism (CDM) studies, Intelligent 
Transport System (ITS) studies,  launching of awareness campaign etc.  in line with the National 

 5
Urban Transport Policy (NUTP), 2006. The objective of this scheme is to guide and facilitate 
implementation of NUTP right form the initia l planning stage. Some proposals have been 
received from States/ULBs only recently under  the new scheme. However, no proposal has 
been approved yet. 
National urban poor fund 
 *143. SHRIMATI T. RATNA BAI: Will the Minister of HOUSING AND URBAN POVERTY 
ALLEVIATION be pleased to state: 
 (a)  whether Government is setting up a National Urban Poor Fund; 
 (b)  if so, the details ther eof and the purpose behind it; 
 (c)  whether the master plans had neglecte d the needs of the informal sector, which 
engages 92 per cent of the total workforce in cities  and towns, especially in the coastal areas of 
Andhra Pradesh; 
 (d)  if so, the details thereof; and 
 (e)  the steps to be taken in this direction? 
 THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINI STRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN POVERTY 
ALLEVIATION (KUMARI SELJA): (a) and (b) The Guidelines of the sub-mission of Basic 
Services to Urban Poor (BSUP) under the Jawaharlal Nehru National Urban Renewal Mission 
(JNNURM), launched on 3rd December 2005, envisa ge the establishment of Basic Services to 
the Urban Poor Fund at the State level. The Gu idelines envisage that wherever state Level  
Nodal Agency releases Central and State funds to  the implementing agencies as soft loan or 
grant-cum-loan, it would ensure that at least 10  per cent of the funds released are recovered 
and ploughed into a revolving fund. This fund would be utilized to meet operation and 
maintenance expenses of the assets created un der the sub-mission. At the end of the Mission 
period, the Revolving, Fund may be graduated to State Basic Services to the Urban Poor Fund. 
 Mandatory reforms given in the guidelines fo r Basic Services to the Urban Poor (BSUP) 
also provide for the internal earmarking with in Urban Local Body (ULB) budgets for basic 
services to the urban poor. Th e Government of India has ad dressed State Governments for 
earmarking at least 25 per cent of municipal budget  for the purpose, eventually leading to the 
creation of a Basic Services to the Urban Poor Fund at the ULB level. 
 In the background of the funds to be establis hed at the State and ULB levels for provision of 
basic services to the urban poor, a Basic Services to the Urban Poor fund is contemplated at the 
national level, seeking support of multilateral and bilateral agencies. The objective of this fund is 
to provide financial support for basic minimum am enities like water supply and sanitation for the 
urban poor/slum-dwellers in a time-bound manner. 
 (c) to (e) The Master plans of cities and to wns across the country, in general, have not 
kept pace with the growth in the informal urban economy and of urban poor needs. The 
Jawaharlal Nehru National Renewal Mission  (JNN URM),  provides for the earmarking at  least 

 6
  
20-25% of developed land in all housing projec ts (both by public and private agencies) for 
Economically weaker Sections (EWS), Low Income Group (LIG) category with a system of 
cross subsidization as part of the Reform agenda to be carried out at the State level. 
 The Prime Minister and Minister of State (I /C) for Housing and Urban Poverty Alleviation 
have addressed Chief Ministers of States to take steps to provide basic entitlements and 
amenities to the urban poor, including land tenure and affordable housing, in a time-bound 
manner. 
Dialogue with Foreign Minister of Pakistan 
 *144. SHRIMATI SUPRIYA SULE: 
  SHRI GIREESH KUMAR SANGHI: 
 Will the Minister of EXTERNAL AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
 (a)  whether Foreign Ministers of India an d Pakistan met in May, 2008 to continue the 
unfinished dialogue; 
 (b)  if so, whether there was also a meetin g on Indo-Pak anti-terror mechanism in the 
month of October, 2008; 
 (c)  if so, the main subjects discussed thereat; 
 (d)  whether any agreement in regard to m eeting the threat of terror has been reached; 
 (e)  if so, to what extent both countries have implemented the proposals;  
and 
 (f)  to what extent anti-terror mechanism of India and Pakistan has been successful? 
 THE MINISTER OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS (SHRI PRANAB MUKHERJEE): (a)  Yes, Sir.  
 (b) Yes, Sir. 
 (c) to (e) The Joint Anti Terrorism Mechan ism had discussed the bombing of the Indian 
Embassy in Kabul and other issues of concern. No response has been received from Pakistan on 
the details on the attack on the Embassy prov ided to it. Government awaits Pakistan's 
response. 
 (f) The joint Anti Terrorism Mechanism unfort unately has not delivered desired results on 
its mandate.

Funds for national highway projects 
 *146. SHRI V. HANUMANTHA RAO: 
  DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY: 
 Will the Minister of SHIPPING, ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be pleased to  
state: 
 (a)  whether in order to attract companies to  invest in Highway projects, his Ministry has 
approached the Finance Ministry seeking low cost funds; 
 (b)  whether a special window from the RBI that would provide for extension of 
reasonable interest rates for highway projects was also considered; 
 (c)  if so, the projects that are being delaye d due to want of funds and to what  extent 
Government has agreed to provide funds to these projects; 

 8
 (d)  by what time they are likely to be completed; 
 (e)  whether National Highways Authority of India has agreed to abandon two projects at 
Vijayawada and Machilipatnam; and 
 (f)  if so, the reasons therefor? 
 THE MINISTER OF SHIPPING, ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS (SHRI T.R. BAALU): 
(a) and (b) The Ministry of Finance has been requested for considering assured flow of credit at 
reasonable interest rate to the projects in road  sector. Government has decided to authorise the 
India Infrastructure Finance Company Limited (I IFCL) to raise Rs. 10,000 crore through tax-free 
bonds by 31.3.2009 to be used for refinancing bank lending of longer maturity to eligible 
infrastructure projects, including highways, in particular. Under this initiative, the IIFCL resources 
used for refinance would leverage bank financing of double the amount to support a PPP 
programme of Rs.100,000 crore in the highways sector. 
 (c) Work on the following five projects under National Highways Development Project 
(NHDP) Phase-V has not commenced on the scheduled appointed date, as these projects have 
not achieved the financial closure : (i) Surat-Da hisar, (ii) Panipat-Jalandhar, (iii) Chennai-
Tada, (iv) Gurgaon-Jaipur and (v) Vijayawada-Chilakaluripet. The Government provides 
Viability Gap Funding (VGF) for projects undertaken on Public-Private-Partnership (PPP) basis. 
However, these five projects have been awarded on revenue sharing basis and do not require 
any VGF.  
 (d) The projects under NHDP Phase-V are scheduled for completion by December, 
2012. 
 (e) No, Sir. 
 (f)  Does not arise. 
Discussion to counter terrorism 
 *147. SHRI JESUDASU SEELAM SUPRIYA: Will the Minister of EXTERNAL AFFAIRS be 
pleased to state: 
 (a)  whether Governments of India and Nepal have met and discussed the steps to 
counter-terror; 
 (b) if so, the main points discussed; 
 (c)  whether effective cooperation for combatin g terrorist activities, including the activities 
of the Indian Insurgent Group operating from Ne pal and the Himalayan nation being used as a 
major transit point for circulation of fake Indian currency notes in India, were also discussed; 
 (d)  if so, the outcome of the talks held; and 
 (e) to what extent India and Nepal have take n steps to check the terror activities in both 
the countries? 

 9
 THE MINISTER OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS (SHR I PRANAB MUKHERJEE): (a) to (e) There 
has been a regular dialogue between the Governme nt of India and the Government of Nepal on 
handling cross-border crimes and security concerns. 
 The institutionalized bilateral mechanism of Ho me Secretaries talks looks into these issues. 
The last round of Home Secretaries talks were held in New Delhi on October 31-November 1, 
2008, in accordance with the decision s reached during the official vi sit of the Prime Minister of 
Nepal to India in September, 2008. During the Home Secretaries talks, both sides discussed 
enhancing ongoing efforts to control activities of  criminal and anti-social elements along the 
India-Nepal border. They  stressed the need for cooperation and information sharing between 
law enforcement agencies of both countries in combating trans-border crimes, and agreed to 
take measures for better coordination in intelligen ce sharing. In order to effectively counter the 
menace of fake currency, both sides agreed to initiate capacity building programmes to enhance 
the capability of enforcement agencies in this area and in tackling money laundering, cyber crime 
and financing of terrorism.  
 During the official visit of External Affairs Minister to Nepal from 24-26 November,  2008, 
both sides agreed to take necessary steps, base d on agreements reached at the last round of 
Home Secretaries talks. 
Coal shortage in NTPC 
 *148. DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY: Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state: 
 (a)  whether there is a coal shortage in the country and National Thermal Power 
Corporation (NTPC) and State Power firms have a pproached his Ministry to meet the shortage 
of coal in power projects; 
 (b)  whether all the power projects  have been facing coal shortage; 
 (c)  whether the Board of Coal India Ltd. ha s approved a first ever proposal to import 
coal; 
 (d)  if so, the total coal to be imported; 
 (e)  the total requirements; and 
 (f)  to what extent import of coal would meet the shortage? 
 THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COAL (SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA): (a) 
and (b) As per Annual Plan 2008-09, Planning Commission envisaged some gap between 
estimated demand of coal for power utilities and source-wise availability including that from Coal 
India Limited (CIL) and Singareni Collieries Co mpany Limited (SCCL). Therefore, keeping in 
view estimated production and expected power generation targets as well as with a view to build 
the coal stocks at power plants, Ministry of Powe r  w a s  a d v i s e d  t o  r e t a i n  l a s t  y e a r ' s  t a r g e t  o f   
20 million tonnes for imports  by power utilities during 2008-09.  Inspite of CIL and SCCL meeting 

 10
their Annual Action Plan (AAP) targets of supply to power utilities during April-November 2008, 
due to lesser materialization as against quarte rly planned movement of coal on account of 
various factors including loading/unloading and movement constraints, short-term production 
constraints in the linked source, increase in Plan t Load Factor (PLF), increase in consumption 
of coal per unit of power genera tion and lesser materialization of targetted imports by power 
utilities, there has been an overall depletion of coal stocks at the power plants. 
 (c) to (f) During the meeting convened in  Planning Commission in September, 2008,  
inter-alia, the position relating to supply of coal to power utilities during 2008-09 having regard 
to projected demand of power utilities and su pply of coal from various sources including 
targetted import was discussed and it was decided that to meet power generation target and 
to have some cushion in coal supplies, addition al 11 million tonnes was to be imported, out of 
which CIL was advised to import 4 million tonnes.  CIL Board has approved import of 4 million 
tonnes of coal by CIL for power utilities during November, 2008 March, 2009. Since the overall 
requirement of power utilities during 2008-09 has b een  estimated at 373 m illion tonnes, it is 
expected that with planned pr oduction and the targ etted imports by power utilities and CIL, 
sufficient coal would be available for meeting power generation requirements in the country 
during 2008-09. 
Marine emergency relief fund 
 *149. SHRI M.V. MYSURA REDDY: Will the Minister of SHIPPING, ROAD TRANSPORT 
AND HIGHWAYS be pleased to state: 
 (a)  whether it is a fact that the number of marine casualties, loss of ships in the Indian 
territorial waters etc. have gone up in the last few years; 
 (b)  if so, whether it is a fact that his Mi nistry has decided to create Marine Emergency 
Relief Fund to address the above and other issues; 
 (c)  whether it is also a fact that a Committee  of Experts has been set up to look into all 
these aspects; and 
 (d)  if so, the details of recommendations made by the Committee? 
 THE MINISTER OF SHIPPING, ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS (SHRI T.R. BAALU): 
(a) Yes, Sir. 
 (b) A Proposal for creation of Marine Emergency Fund is under consideration. 
 (c) and (d) A "Committee on urgent measures  for prevention of marine casualties and 
emergency response" has studied and made recommendations on the measures to reduce the 
marine casualties in the Indian coastal wate rs. The recommendations made by the Committee 
include preventive and rehabilitation measures including restriction on old vessels; stringent 
inspections and creation of Emergency Fund. Th e Committee has also made recommendations 
for an emergency response mechanism for responding  in  emergency situations;  salvage and oil 

 11 
pollution recovery mechanism. Various other meas ures including making appropriate legislative 
changes to deal with the emergency situations have also been recommended. 
Land management in major ports 
 *150. SHRI RAJEEV SHUKLA: Will the Minister of SHIPPING, ROAD TRANSPORT AND 
HIGHWAYS be pleased to state: 
 (a)  whether he has written to the Indian Ports Association to prepare a comprehensive 
information system on land management pattern in major ports of the country; 
 (b)  if so, whether response has been received from the association; 
 (c)  if so, the concrete measures and steps hi s Ministry is considering to take to improve 
the major ports in the country; 
 (d)  whether all the State Governments conc erned have to provide more land, etc. for 
development of ports; and 
 (e) whether the Union Government has approved Rs. 1008 crores for development of 
these projects? 
 THE MINISTER OF SHIPPING, ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS (SHRI T.R BAALU): 
(a) and (b) The Union Ministry for Shipping has requested Indian Ports Association (IPA) to 
evaluate the online system of land management of  Tuticorin Port Trust. The Tuticorin Port Trust 
has recently introduced an online system to monitor and handle its land in order to bring 
transparency which includes digitization of all pl ots of land with its status and classification, 
automatic generation of alert message and online request for processing. The Indian Ports 
Association has been asked to evaluate this onlin e  s y s t e m  a n d  m a k e  n e c e s s a r y  s t u d y ,  i f  i t  i s  
workable, so that it could be implemented in all major Port Trusts. 
 (c) Improvement/modernization of ports is a continuous process where various projects 
are taken up by the individual ports based on their requirement and forecast. The Department of 
Shipping has formulated a National Maritime Development Programme (NMDP) for 
modernization of the Port sector of facilitat e enhanced private inve stment, improve service 
quality and promote competitiveness. Under the NM DP, 276 projects have been identified in the 
port sector for implementation in the Major ports which are to be taken up in a period from 2004-
05 to 2011-12. These projects cover the entire gamut of activities in the port sector which include 
berth development, deepening of channel, procurement of equipment and port craft, rail/road 
connectivity and other associated work. Till date 36 projects of the port sector with total cost of 
Rs.3930 crores have been completed under NMDP. 
 (d) and (e) No, Sir.

 THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PLANNING (SHRI V.

below or above the poverty line. The poverty line is different in the rural and urban areas and 
within each area the poverty lines differ amon g the states. The poverty line in 1973-74 has 
been expressed in terms of per capita consum ption expenditure of Rs.49.09 per month in the 
rural areas and Rs.56.64 per month in the urban areas at 1973-74 pieces at the national level

calorie requirement of 2400 kcal in the rural areas and 2100 kcal in the urban areas. These

specific poverty lines, using state-specific price indices and inter-state price differentials 
following the methodology contained in the Repo rt of the Expert Group on Estimation of 
proportion and number of Poor (Lakdawala Committee). The latest estimate of state-wise 
poverty lines available for the year 2004–05 is given in the Statement ( See below). The 
poverty line in the states ranges from Rs.292 .95 to Rs.478.02 in the rural areas and from 
Rs.378.84 to Rs.665.90 in the urban areas. 
 The Planning Commission estimates percenta ge and number of people living below and 
above the poverty line from the large sample survey on household consumer expenditure 
conducted by the National Sample Survey Organiza tion (NSSO) at an interval of approximately 
five years following the methodology contained in the report of the Expert Group on estimation of 
proportion and number of poor. As per the latest estimate, available for the year 2004–05 based 
on the large sample survey of consumer expe nditure data of the 61st Round (July 2004—June 
2005) of the NSSO, 795.4 million persons (72.5% of the total population) lived above the

per day.

Ganga action plan 
 1129. SHRI BANWARI LAL KANCHHAL: Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state: 
 (a)  whether more than Rs. 1000 crore have been spent on the Ganga Action Plan (GAP) 
project to clean it but the holy river Ganga still remains heavily polluted; 
 (b)  if so, the reasons fo r the failure of GAP; and 
 (c)  whether there is any proposal to fix ac countability of the agencies etc., who failed to 
execute GAP in its true spirit?  
 THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINIST RY OF ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS (SHRI 
NAMO NARAIN MEENA): (a) to (c) The Ganga Action Plan (GAP) Phase I, the first attempt as 
a centrally funded scheme for ri ver conservation was launched in the year 1985. The Plan was 
taken up to treat partial pollution load to the river. Under this Plan, 260 pollution abatement 
schemes spread over 25 towns in the States of  Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and West Bengal were 
completed at an expenditure of Rs.452 crore le ading to the creation of additional sewage 
treatment capacity of 469 million litres per da y (mld). GAP Phase-I was declared closed in 
March, 2000. Since GAP Phase-I did not cover the pollution load of Ganga fully, GAP Phase II 
which included Plans for Yamuna, Gomti, Damodar and Mahananda besides Ganga was 
approved in various stages from 1993 onwards.  The present sanctioned cost of works for 

 71
Ganga river (main stem) under GA P Phase-II is Rs. 564 crore against which an amount of  
Rs. l373.58 crore has been released to the State Implementing Agencies. Out of a total of  
311 schemes sanctioned, 185 schemes have been completed so far and the balance schemes 
are in different stages of implementation. 
 With the completion of the pollution abatement works under GAP Phase-I and II, 
notwithstanding the phenomenal increase in the urban population leading to substantial increase 
in the pollution load of the river Ganga over the past year, water quality of Ganga has shown 
improvement at major locations over its pre- GAP quality in terms of Biochemical Oxygen 
Demand (BOD). The BOD values in the year 2008 range between 1.2 to 4.8 mg./litre in major 
monitoring locations as compared to BOD values ranging between 1.7 to 15.5 mg./litre in 1986. 
This is as per the water qualit y monitoring undertaken by independent reputed institutions like 
the Central Pollution Control Board  (CPCB), Bh arat Heavy Electricals Ltd. (BHEL), Indian 
Institute of Technology (IIT), Kanpur and In dian Toxicological Research Centre (ITRC), 
Lucknow. 
 The Government has initiated an exercise for revamping the Ganga Action Plan with a view 
to promoting a holistic and integrated approach.

Pollution in rivers 
 1138.  KUMAR DEEPAK DAS: Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state: 
 (a)  whether it is a fact that pollution has been increasing in various rivers including 
Brahmaputra through its tributaries like Bharaba river in Guwahati city;

 (c)  if not, the reasons therefor? 
 THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINI STRY OF ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS  
(SHRI NAMO NARAIN MEENA): (a) to (c) The Government has taken steps for pollution 
abatement in the identified stretches of the major rivers. The rivers conservation efforts in this 
direction commenced with the launching of the Ganga Action Plan (GAP) phase-I in the year 
1985. GAP Phase-I was extended to GAP phase-II in various stages during 1993-96 to cover 
various tributaries of the river Ganga. GAP phas e-II was merged in late 1996 with the National 
River Conservation Plan (NRCP) which presently covers identified polluted stretches of 35 rivers  
and 164 towns spread over 20 States. The Pollution abatement works undertaken in these towns 
†Original notice of the question was received in Hindi. 

 77
under NRCP include interception and diversion works to capture the raw sewage flowing into the 
river through open drains and divert them for treatment in Sewage Treatment Plants; Low Cost 
Sanitation works on river banks; Electric and/or improved  wood-crematoria for proper 
cremation of bodies; River Front Development works, Public Participation and Awareness 
programmes etc. As per the Water Quality Monitoring undertaken through reputed independent 
Institutions, water quality in the river Ganga has improved  in terms of values of the Bio-chemical 
Oxygen Demand (BOD) compared to pre-GAP pe riod. Similarly in the case of Yamuna, the 
water quality is conforming to the prescribed lim its except for the stretch of Delhi and parts of 
Uttar Pradesh mainly due to extraction of water from Yamuna for drinking purposes. 
 River conservation is a mammoth task requir ing involvement of all the stakeholders. The 
Central Government supplements the efforts of  the State Governments in creation of civic 
infrastructure for sewage management and disposal  etc. by providing grant for capital works in 
the identified polluted stretches. There are also other Central programmes presently in operation 
under the Union Ministry of Urban Development, namely, the Jawaharlal Nehru National Urban 
Renewal Mission (JNNURM) and the Urban Infrastructure Development Scheme for Small and 
Medium Towns (UIDSSMT), for supplementing the efforts of the State Governments and Urban 
Local Bodies by provision of Additional Centra l Assistance (ACA) as pe r guidelines of these 
programmes. Sewerage and sewage treatment ( i.e. domestic wastewater treatment) are 
among the admissible components under these programmes. The Government has also initiated 
an exercise for revamping the river conservation  strategy to promote a holistic and integrated 
approach. 
 The rivers taken up for pollution abatement works under NRCP do not include the river 
Brahamaputra. The water quality of the river, as per the available reports conforms to the 
prescribed bathing standards under NRCP for organic pollution level.

Statement 
 A brief overview of the schemes initiated by the Ministry of Overseas Indian Affairs and 
their salient features: 
1. Overseas Citizenship of India (OCI)  
 The objective of the scheme is to fulfill th e aspirations and expectations of Overseas 
Indians. This will bring Overseas Indian Community closer to the country and will 
enable them to participate in the development programmes more effectively. 
2. Know India Programme (Internship Programme for Diaspora Youth)  
 The objective is to bring the young overseas Indians closer and bond with 
contemporary India. It helps the younger generation of overseas Indians understand 
India better. It also provides a forum for students and young professionals of Indian 
origin to share their views, expect ations and experience and bond with 
contemporary India. 
3. Scholarship Scheme for Diaspora Children (SSDC).  
 The objective of the scheme is to improv e the relationship between and   Overseas 
Indian Community and help the deserving students. Students selected  for such 
scholarships become brand ambassadors fo r India and its educational institutions 
and help in deepening the relationships between India and the Overseas Indian 
Community. 
4. Awareness Campaign/Media Plan  
 The objective of the scheme is to promot e legal migration, create awareness among 
potential emigrants, spreading awarene ss among the masses about fraudulent 
practices of touts/unregistered Recruiti ng Agents (RAs) and making prospective 
brides of NRIs aware of the fraudulent marriages. 
5. Pre-departure orientation and skill up gradation for emigrant workers  
 The objective of the scheme is to prepare the Indian workers to take up skilled  jobs 

 104 
in overseas employment market and create better skilled and more competitive 
emigrants work force. 
6. Legal assistance to women facing problems in NRI marriages 
 The objective of the scheme is to help the Indian women deserted by their Overseas 
Indian Husbands. 
7. E-Governance in emigration  
 The objective of the scheme is automation and computerization of Protector of 
Emigrant (POE) offices. All POE offices have been computerized. 
  In addition to the above, Ministry of Overseas Indian Affairs extends a wide variety 
of services to overseas Indians in social, ec onomic and cultural matters. The Ministry has 
the following programmes: 
1. India Development Foundation   
 The objective is to involve Overseas Indian s in the social development of India. The 
projected outcome is to channelise Overseas Indian Resources into social sectors. 
2. Overseas Indian Facilitation Center (OIFC)  
 The objective is to promote investment in  India by Overseas Indians. The projected 
outcomes are Promotion and facilitation of a two way flow of Overseas Indian 
Investment into India as well as business-to-business partnerships of Indian 
business houses with Overseas Indians. 
3. Overseas Workers Resource Centre (OWRC)  
 The objective is to create awareness among potential emigrants and disseminate 
information. The projected outcomes ar e Information dissemination on matters 
relating to emigration, monitoring complaints received from emigrants workers, 
grievance redressal and follow up with various stakeholders. 
4. Overseas Indian Centers  
 The aim is to start three centers in Duba i, Washington and Kuala Lumpur with the 
objective to extend a host of counseling se rvices to Overseas Indian Workers. The 
centers will provide legal, medical, financ ial and counseling services to the Indian 
workers. 
5. Setting up Council for Promotion of Overseas Employment (CPOE)  
 The objective is forecasting of future  opportunities for overseas employment, 
projection and plans for overseas deployment of workers, disseminating information 
and upgrading skills of intending emigrants.  The likely outcomes of this programme 
is benchmarking, testing and certification of  skills, imparting foreign language skills 
and on-site welfare measures for emigrants. 

 105
6. Construction of the Prav asi Bharatiya Kendra (PBK) 
 The objective is to commemorate the ev olution and achievements of the India 
Diaspora. PBK would become the hub of va rious activities aimed at harnessing the 
talent pool among the Indian Diaspora and developing a sense of pride in the 
achievements of India and the Diaspora. This will also provide better work 
environment to the staff and better facilities to the general public. 
7. Celebration of Pravasi Bharatiya Diwas (PBD)  
 The objective is to organize the annual PBD for creating a platform for bringing 
Overseas Indians from variou s countries together to sh are their experiences, and 
integrating it with the Country's developm ent process. The projected outcome is to 
develop a bond and unity of purpose. Six Pravasi Bharatiya Diwas have been 
organized so far.

 (iii) In respect of complaint against the foreign employer (FE), FE is placed in the prior 
approval category (Black list) and as a consequence is not allowed to recruit 
workers from India. 
 (iv) In case the stay of the Indian emigrant worker is declared illegal on account of various 
reasons, the Indian Missions take up the matter with the local authorities for either 
regularizing their stay or their safe deportation back to India. 
 (v) In case deportation is required, this Ministry coordinates with the local Government 
through Indian Missions, the state government authorities, Ministries of Home Affairs 
and External Affairs for ensuring their safe passage back to India. 
 (vi) Special measures being taken for better protection and welfare of vulnerable sections 
of emigrants including women emigrants are : 
  1. Age restriction of 30 years for all women emigrating on ECR passports. 
  2. Opening of Overseas Indian Workers Re source Centre in host countries to serve 
as a one stop service outlet for addressing the information and assistance needs 
of emigrants. 
  3. A 24x7 helpline viz. Overseas Workers Resource Centre (OWRC) has been set 
up to enable emigrants/prospective em igrants to seek information and file 
complaints against Recruiting Agents/ Foreign Employers. 

 107
 (vii) A comprehensive insurance scheme, viz. Pravasi Bharatiya Bima Yojana, 2006, is in 
place, which makes it mandatory for every emigrant worker to be covered under the 
Scheme while seeking emigration clearance. The Scheme, inter-alia, provides 
workers with life insurance, medical expenses and legal expenses cover and also the 
deportation expenses wherever needed. Wi th effect from 01.04.2008, the scheme 
has been upgraded by providing addition al benefits at reduced premium rates. 
Workers now have life insurance coverage of Rs.10 lakhs (in place of Rs.5 lakhs), 
Medical Expenses coverage of Rs.75,000/ - (in place of Rs.50,000/-), Family 
Hospitalization coverage of Rs.50,000/ - (in place of Rs.25,000/-), Maternity 
Expenses coverage of Rs.25,000/- (in pl ace of Rs.20,000/-), Legal Expenses 
coverage of Rs. 30,000/- (in place of Rs.25,000/-) etc. The insurance premium has 
been reduced to Rs.275 for 2 years policy period and Rs.375 for 3 years policy 
period. 
 (viii) A vigorous campaign in the print and el ectronic media to educate potential emigrants 
including labourers and other vulnerable sections like women emigrants has been 
launched to propagate the benefits and hazards of legal and illegal migration 
respectively. 
 (ix) This Ministry has signed bilateral MOUs  with the UAE, Kuwait and Oman and 
additional protocol on the existing MoU wi th Qatar to ensure protection to emigrant 
workers. MoU with Malaysia and Bahrain ha ve been finalized. Efforts are being made 
to sign MoUs with other labour receiving countries. These MOUs provide for a Joint 
Committee consisting of representatives of  both countries to discuss and resolve 
grievances of workers.

especially at the grassroots leve l and the poor access to competit ive sports. The Government is

Abhiyan (PYKKA). PYKKA aims to cover all the pa nchayats in the country in a phased manner 
over a period of 10 years. Besides, promoting mass  participation, this Scheme is also expected 
to expand the talent pool by tapping the hitherto largely unexploited rural sports talent.

responsibility of the National Sports Federation s (NSFs) concerned. However, the Government 
appoints observers to oversee the selection proces s with a view to ensuring that the selection 
process is fair and transparent. Assistance is rele ased only after ensuring that the selection has

 (c) and (d) The Government of  India has been liberally funding the State Government for 
implementing various schemes for handloom weavers to address the felt needs of the handloom 
weavers to enhance their production, productivity and enhance the income and social economic 
status of the weavers by providing skill up-gradati on, infrastructure and input supply support to 
them. During the 11th Five Year  Plan, the Office of Development Commissioner for Handlooms 
has been implementing 5 Schemes viz. (1) Integrated Handlooms Development Schemes,  
(2) handlooms Weavers Comprehensive Welfare Scheme which consisted of Health Insurance 
Scheme and Mahatma Gandhi Bunkar Bima Yojn a, (3) Mill Gate Price Scheme, (4) Marketing 
and Export Promotion Scheme, (5) diversified Handloom Development Scheme. 
 The Government of India is implementing In tegrated Handloom Development scheme since 
2007-08 for Integrated and holistic development of  the handloom clusters. As per the Scheme, 
the cluster should have 300-500 looms and is to be  developed in a time frame of three years at 
an upper cost of Rs. 60.00 lakh per cluster. On e of the components of the Scheme is "Corpus 
Fund for Setting-up of yarn Depot", for which financial assistance of Rs. 3.00 lakh provided to 
ensure supply of yarn to the handloom weavers through the yarn depot at the cluster. Under the 
Scheme, so far 367 clusters have been sanctioned. 
 The Government of India is also impl ementing Mill Gate Price Scheme since  
1992-93 with the objective of providing all types of yarn to the eligible Handloom Weavers at mill 
gate price. The Scheme is being implemen ted through National Handloom Development 
Corporation (NHDC). The expenditure involved for transporting the yarn from the Mill Gate to 
the Godown of the handloom agen cies is reimbursed to the ha ndloom agencies. At present, 
yarn is being supplied under Mill Gate Price Scheme throughout the country through 485 Yarn 
Depots. During the year 2007-08, 687.46 lakh kgs. of yarn has been supplied. 
 The Government of India is implementing Health Insurance Scheme from 2005-06. The 
scheme covers not only the weaver but his wife and two children also. The ancillary handloom 
workers like those engaged in warping, winding, dyeing., printing, finishing, sizing, Jhala 
making, Jacquard cutting etc. are also eligible  to be covered under the scheme. The scheme 
covers all pre-existing diseases as well as ne w diseases and a substantial provision has been 
kept for OPD. The annual limit per family is  Rs. 15,000/- out of whic h OPD cover will be Rs. 
7500/-. During the year 2007-08, 17.74 lakh weavers have been enrolled under the Health 
Insurance Scheme.

 THE MINISTER OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT (SHRI RAGHUVANSH PRASAD SINGH): (a) 
Yes, Sir. NREGA is demand based programme. In  the current financial year at B.E. stage, 
budget provision of Rs. 16000 crore had been made for implementation of the Act. However, in 
view of the rising labour demand in various St ates, an additional grant of Rs. 10500 crore has 
been made available. 
 (b) On a request made by the Ministry of Rural Development, C and AG conducted 
performance audit of the implementation of NREG A in 26 States covering 68 district, 141 blocks 
and 568 Gram Panchayats for the period from Fe bruary, 2006 to March, 2007. Final audit report 
of C and AG has been laid on the Table of the House on 24.10.2008. 
 Findings of CAG as given in its final report re late mainly to issues such as application for 
employment, issue of dated receipts, job card formats, muster rolls, maintenance of record 
registers, delayed payment of wages, lack of an effective grievance redressal system, inspection 
of works, monitoring and shortage of staff wi th the implementing agencies, expenditure on  
non-permissible activities/ineligible persons/agencies and incorrect accounting of expenditure. 
 (c) and (d) CAG report has been shared with the States. At Central level, the Ministry has 
taken the following steps for smooth and effective implementation of NREG Act. 
 (i) Generating Awareness 
  Various steps have been taken to generate awareness about NREGA. Gram Sabhas 
and one day orientation of all Sarpanches at the Block level have been held. Local 
vernacular newspapers, radio, TV, films an d cultural forms are being used for the 
purpose. Leaflets and brochures in local language are being provided. Village camps 
have been organized by the District teams and NGOs and Self help Groups are being 
associated in the awareness generation. 

 191
 (ii) Staffing/Training  
  Capacity building for rural development functionaries and Panchayati Raj functionaries 
is an essential pre-requisite for better  implementation of rural development 
programmes. NREGA guidelines provide th at a dedicated Gram Rozgar Sahayak 
(GRS) should be appointed in each Gram Panchayat and a dedicated Programme 
officer should be appointed at Block leve l for NREGA works besides other technical 
and non-technical staff. So far 1.92 lakh GRS and 5454 Programme Officers have been 
recruited. Besides, 23196 technical staff and 12325 other non-technical staff has also 
been recruited for NREGA. As regards training, 7.19 lakh Panchayati Raj functionaries, 
1.64 lakh GRS, 19687 technical staff, 11238 no n-technical staff and 6.17 lakh Members 
of Vigilance and Monitoring Committees (VMC) have been trained under NREGA. 
 (iii) People's Participation 
 (a) Village level monitoring committees have been set up and trained. 
 (b) Non Government Organisations are be ing involved for awareness generation 
under NREGA. The Government of India ha s introduced awards to be known as 
Rozgar Jagrookta Puraskar (Employment awareness awards) to recognize the 
outstanding contribution by the civil soci ety organisations for promoting effective 
implementation of NREGA in different states of the country. 
 (c) Gram Sabhas are held. 
 (iv) Vigilance and Monitoring 
  Implementation of NREG Act is monitored on regular basis. Vigilance and Monitoring 
Committees have been set up at State as we ll as district levels. Local MPs are the 
members of the district Vigilance and Moni toring Committees. Village level Vigilance 
and Monitoring Committees have also been set up for local monitoring. Members of 
the Central Employment Guarantee Council under take field visits to  various districts. 
National level Monitors (NLMs) and Area Offi cers visit various districts to oversee the 
progress of the Act. Performance of NREGA is  reviewed periodically by Minister (RD) 
and Secretary (RD) during fortnightly meetings, Performance Review Committee 
meetings and State specific review meetings. 
 (v) Transparency 
 (a) States have been requested to make payment of wages to NREGA workers 
through their accounts in Post Offices/Ban ks. So far 4.92 crore Post Office/bank 
accounts of NREGA workers have been opened. 
 (b) States have been directed to conduc t social audit of each and every work of 
NREGA within three months. Members of the Central Employment Guarantee 
Council are actively participating the Social  Audit. Social Audit has been done in 
1.5 lakh Gram Panchayats. 

 192
 (c) A comprehensive Web-based MIS www. nrega.nic.in has been implemented 
which places all data in public domain. 
  State have been asked to put all Muster Rolls (MR) on the web site of NREGA 
and make on-line reporting of the MRs ve rified and works inspected at block and 
district level. So far, 95.49 lakh MRs have been verified, 2.29 lakh works have 
been inspected at district level and 14.07 lakh works have been inspected at block 
level. 
 (d) A Citizen Information Board has been introduced. This board is to be displayed at 
all prominent places. This will enable th e local community to know the works 
being undertaken under NREGA and would also facilitate the process of spreading 
awareness about the programme. 
 (vi) Grievance redressal mechanism 
  A grievance redressal mechanism has been set up. A helpline has also been 
established and made operational in the Mi nistry to address the public complaints/ 
grievances and to provide general informat ion about NREGA. States have also been 
advised to put up their helplines.

 936. SHRI C. RAMACHANDRAIAH : Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY be 
pleased to state :

these items were found contaminated in China; 
 (b) whether steps are being taken to effectively implement the above ban; 
 (c) if so, the details thereof; and 
 (d) if not, the reasons therefor? 
 THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE DE PARTMENT OF COMMER CE, MINISTRY OF 
COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY (SHRI JAIRAM RAMESH): (a) Directorate General of Foreign 
Trade (DGFT) has prohibited import of milk and milk products from China upto 23rd June, 2009.

milk or milk solids as an ingredient from China has also been prohibited for six months vide

 204

three months.

Health Authorities to monitor melamine contamination in foods and to take special care and

be pleased to state :

during the last three decades;

of steel into India;

steel manufacturers to curb large scale import of steel?

Iron ore exports are carried out only after meetin g the domestic requirement. Even after exports 
and meeting domestic requirements, still surpluses are left. The import of finished steel in 2007-
08 was approximately 7 million tonnes while it is 3.3 million tonnes in the first seven months of the 
current financial year.

available, Government has canalised export of iron ore with Fe content of above 64%. 
Presently, as the domestic price of high grade ore is the main issue as far as steel manufacturers

Restricting export of iron ore 
 939. SHRIMATI JAYA BACHCHAN: Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY be 
pleased to state: 
 (a) whether it is a fact that country’s iron ore experts have advised on restricting or 
stopping altogether the export of iron ore as it is considered worse than selling family silver; 
 (b) the factors that prevent us from selling it at  best prices in the world than dumping it at 
cheapest prices; 
 (c) if so, whether Government has taken  any decision on export of iron ore; and 
 (d) if not, the reasons therefor? 
 THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE DE PARTMENT OF COMMER CE, MINISTRY OF 
COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY (SHRI JAIRAM RAMESH): (a) An expert Committee, constituted 
by the Central Government, examined the issu e of restrictions on iron ore export. The 
Committee consulted the various stakeholders in cluding State Governments and submitted its 
report which was considered by the Government. Government agreed to the recommendation of 
the expert Committee that restrictions on export of iron ore are not required, while holding that 
even though conservation of iron ore resources of the country is of paramount importance, the 
same may not be achieved by banning or capping th e export of iron ore but by taking recourse 
to appropriate fiscal measures. 

 207
 (b) Indian ore in the export market till very  recently was very competitively priced. For 
instance, in the month of April, 2008 the spot price of Indian iron was US$ 145 per metric tonne 
on FOB basis as compared to approximately US $ 134 per metric tonne which was the price of 
iron ore being exported by other countries on long tern agreement basis. However, the spot 
price of Indian ore has come down to US$ 51 per metric tonne on FOB basis in November, 2008 
and the iron ore exports have also come down from 52.65 million tonnes for the period from 1st 
April to 15th November, 2007 to 45.20 million tonnes for the same period during the current 
financial year. 
 (c) and (d) In view of (a) and (b) above, th ere is no change in the policy of Government 
on export of iron ore. 
Impact of FTA with Asian countries 
 940. SHRI K.E. ISMAIL: 
  SHRI D. RAJA: 
 Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state: 
 (a) whether Government has made any study about the impact of Free Trade Agreement 
(FTA) with Asian countries on our industry and agriculture; and 
 (b) if so, the details of the FTAs made so far and the result of the study made? 
 THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE DE PARTMENT OF COMMER CE, MINISTRY OF 
COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY (SHRI JAIRAM RAMESH): (a) Before entering into negotiations 
with its trading partners, studies are undertaken internally, as well as through joint study groups 
to study the feasibility of the proposed FTAs, in cluding their impact on the domestic industry. 
Consultations are also held with  the domestic stakeholders in cluding the Apex Chambers of 
Commerce and Industry, industry as sociations as well as the ad ministrative Mi nistries and 
Departments. In order to protect the interests of the domestic industry, these Agreements 
provide for maintaining sensitive/negative lists of  items on which limited or no tariff concessions 
are granted under the FTA. In addition, in case of a surge in imports and injury to the domestic 
industry, a country is allowed to take measures such as anti-dumping and safeguards. 
 (b) India has signed Free Trade Agre ements with the following countries 
 (i) The India-Sri Lanka Free Trade Agreemen t covering only goods was signed on 28 
December 1998 and its implementation began in March 2000. 
 (ii) India and Singapore have signed a Comprehensive Economic Cooperation Agreement 
(CECA) on 29 June 2005 which became effective from 1 August, 2006. The CECA 
includes, inter-alia, free trade agreements in goods, services and investment. 
 (iii) The Agreement on South Asian Free  Trade Area (SAFTA), covering goods, was 
signed by the SAARC member  countries (Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, 
Nepal, Pakistan and Sri Lanka) during the 12th SAARC Summit in Islamabad on 6 
January 2004 and has come into force from 1 January 2006. The tariff liberalization 
programme under SAFTA has commenced from 1 July 2006.

Support to small tea growers in Assam 
 942.  SHRI BIRENDRA PRASAD BAIS HYA: Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND 
INDUSTRY be pleased to state: 
 (a) the per cent contribution of small tea grow ers in the overall productivity of the country 
with special reference to Assam; 
 (b) the kind of financial and other support Government is extending and proposes to 
extend towards enhancing quality production by small tea growers in Assam; 
 (c) the major constraints of small tea growers in their rapid growth and sustenance; and 
 (d) the steps taken by Governme nt to mitigate their problems? 
 THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE DE PARTMENT OF COMMER CE, MINISTRY OF 
COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY (SHRI JAIRAM RAMESH): (a) The contribution from small tea 
growers to the national tea production is around 250 million kgs and it accounts for nearly 25% 
of the all India tea production of which 10% is accounted for by small growers in Assam. 

 209
 (b) In order to harness the potential econo mic value of the small grower sector, the 
measures adopted by Government are aimed at im proving their farm productivity and quality of 
their produce, and then providing them with a market access to ensure a reasonable return from 
their investments. Focused attention is being pa id to organize the growers into Self Help  
Groups (SHGs) and Financial assistance is being extended to them facilitating establishment of 
proper leaf collection system, transport arrang ements and establishing proper partnership 
arrangements with the quality tea processing factories. 
 (c) The major constraints of small tea grower s are small fragmented holdings scattered in 
remote areas not having land ownership, not conversant with good agricultural practices and not 
having their own processing facility. 
 (d) The self help groups are provided with 100% grant for setting up of leaf collection 
centers, storage godowns, purchasing Leaf weighi ng scales, Plastic crates/nylon leaf carry

pesticides, sprayers etc. A special training on modern aspects of tea growing is organized for 
selected two members from each self help groups who in turn on completi on of the training are 
expected to impart training to other members of the SHG and also take care of the management 
of the tea area under the command of the SHG. Besides Meeting the training fee and boarding 
and lodging cost, each trainee is Provided with stipend @ Rs.500/- per month for next six 
months from the date of completion of the training.

 947. DR. (SHRIMATI) NAJMA A. HEPTULLA: 
  SHRI MAHENDRA MOHAN: 
 Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state: 
 (a) whether it is a fact that trade between India and China will reach more than 20 billion 
dollars during the current financial year; 
 (b) if so, the details thereof; 
 (c) what is trade deficit between India an d China and also with other countries; and 
 (d) how this trade gap will be filled and wh at steps have been taken in this regard? 
 THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE DE PARTMENT OF COMMER CE, MINISTRY OF 
COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY (SHRI JAIRAM RAMESH): (a) and (b) The trade between India 
and China has already crossed US $ 20 billion in the year 2007-08. During 2007-08 the trade 
between India and China was of the volume of US $ 37.9 billion. 
 (c) The trade deficit between India and China during the year 2007-08 was US $ 16.27 
billion. During 2007-08 the trade deficit with South Korea was US $ 3.1 billion and with Japan  
US $ 2.4 billion. 
 (d) The trade gap can be filled by increasing our exports to these countries. During the 
Prime Minister's visit to China in January 2008 th e Commerce and Industry Minister raised the 
issue of growing trade deficit with  his Chinese counterpart. In or der to bridge the trade deficit 
from 2007 onwards China is organising South Asian Commodity fair every year. India Trade

 974.  DR. K. MALAISAMY: Will the Minister of EARTH SCIENCES be pleased to state:

 THE MINISTER OF EARTH SCIENCES (SHRI KAPIL SIBAL): (a) and (b) Yes, Sir. After 
the December 2004 tsunami, the earthquake events  were monitored for their tsunamigenic 
potential in the Indian Ocean since July 2005. Since then nine instances of earthquake of 
magnitude 7.0 and above have been observed in  the Indian Ocean. Out of these, on two 
instances minor changes in sea level were obse rved on the Indian coast and the Andaman and 
Nicobar Islands. No impact was observed all along the Indian coast due to transient minor 
changes of sea level.

Islands are susceptible to tsunamis that may be generated/triggered by the tsunamigenic 
earthquakes (Magnitude 7.0 and abov e) in the two subduction zones, viz. The  
Andaman-Sunda-Sumatra-Java subduction zone and the Makaran subduction zone in the 
Indian Ocean. 
 (d) Yes, Sir. There are scientific devices  to know the occurrence of such event and 
forecast of tsunami in advance, if generated. The Government has established an Early Warning 
System for Tsunami in the Indian Ocean. An Ea rly Warning Centre has been set up at Indian 
National Centre for Ocean  Information  Services (INCOIS),  Hyderabad  and is operational since

15th October 2007 on 24x7 basis. Early Warning Centre receives real time Seismic. Bottom

networks. The progression of the tsunami wave is monitored through the BPRs placed at sea 
bottom in the Bay of Bengal and the Arabian S ea which have real time connectivity with the 
warning system. Seismic, sea-level and BPR data are continuously monitored in the Early

Norms for declaring natural disasters 
 †978. SHRIMATI SUSHMA SWARAJ: Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be pleased to 
state: 
 (a) the norms adopted to declare disaster as natural disaster; 
 (b) whether special concessions are provided  to the concerned State Governments after 
declaration of natural disaster; and 
 (c) whether all these concessions have been provided to Government of Bihar following 
declaration of Bihar flood as natural disaster? 
 THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS (SHRIMATI V. RADHIKA 
SELVI): (a) to (c) Inclusion of a calamity/disaster  in the list of natural disasters eligible for 
assistance from CRF/NCCF comes under the purviews of the successive Finance Commissions. 
The present list of notified natural calamities,  which is based on the Award of 12th Finance 
Commission, consists of cyclone, drought, earthquake/tsunami, fire, flood, hailstorm, landslide, 
avalanche, cloud burst and pest attack. 
 The assistance for relief in the wake of natural calamities is given to the States under the two 
schemes viz. Calamity Relief Fund (CRF) and National Calamity Contingency Fund (NCCF) 
Schemes. The expenditure from CRF/NCCF is re quired to be incurred as per the items and 
norms approved by the Government of India. A CRF has been constituted for each State, which 
is contributed by the Government of India and th e State Governments in ratio of 3:1. The State 
Governments are required to meet expenditure on  relief and rehabilitation out of the corpus of 
the CRF. CRF is a ready availability of fund with the State Government. In case the calamity is of 
a severe nature and the funds available in the St ate's CRF account are not sufficient, additional 
assistance is provided to the States out of the National Calamity Contingency Fund (NCCF), 
after following the established procedure. 
 The event of kosi breach and floods in Northe rn Bihar, is covered under the category of 
'floods', which is one of the notified natural disaster. Financial assistance to the affected States 
including Bihar is being provided as per the above schemes.

 989. DR. V. MAITREYAN: Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
 (a) the overall scenario of the internal security  in the country particularly in the metro cities 
of the country; 
 (b) the steps being taken to contain the terror attacks in the country;

investigated and culprits brought to books;

detection of the antisocial elements attacks on the cities across the country? 
 THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS (SHRI SHRIPRAKASH 
JAISWAL): (a) The overall internal security scenario in the country remains largely under control 
although some metro cities were targeted by the terrorists, recently. 
 (b) to (e) The Government is pursuing a multi- pronged strategy to deal with the challenges 
posed by the activities of terrorists/insurgents/ extremists in various parts of the country, 
including measures on the political, security and development fronts. The various measures 
taken on the security fronts, inter-alia include vigilance and patrolling on the borders to check 
infiltration and illegal cross-border activities, deployment of Central Forces to aid the State Police 
Forces in areas prone to terrorist violence, heig htened vigil and security  arrangements in and 
around vital installations, strengthening of intelligence gathering and sharing capabilities, 
particularly at the cutting edge level, upgradat ion and modernization of Central and State Police 
Forces, assistance for raising India Reserve Ba ttalions, re-imbursement of various types of 
Security Related Expenditure (SRE) to the State Go vernments, various initiatives at the bilateral 
and multi-lateral cooperation to deal with the global imperatives of terrorism. "Public Order" and

 (d)  if not, the way in which Centre directs th e States for the proper usage of the assistance 
or the steps taken by Government? 
 THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS (SHRIMATI V. RADHIKA 
SELVI): (a) to (d) As per the Scheme of financing the relief expenditure, the State 
Governments concerned are primar ily responsible for undertaking necessary relief measures in 
the wake of natural disasters. Distribution of re lief on ground is the responsibility of the State 
Government concerned. The Go vernment of India supplements the efforts of the State 
Governments by providing financial and logistic  support, where necessary. Such support is 
within the framework of Award of the Finance Commissions. A calamity Relief Fund (CRF) has 
been constituted with an allocated amount for each State. The Government of India contributes

 75% of the CRF and the State Government contributes the remaining 25%. As such the State 
Governments have a readily availability of funds is CRF account for immediate relief operations. 
The State Level Committee headed by the Chief Secr etary is fully authorized to decide on all 
matters relating to the financing of the relief expenditure from the CRF in accordance with the 
items and norms approved by the Government of In dia. In  the event of a calamity of a severe 
nature, in which the requirement of funds for relief operations is beyond the funds available in the 
States, CRF account, additional Ce ntral assistance is also considered from National Calamity 
Contingency Fund (NCCF), after following the laid down procedure. 
 The quantum of fund to various States in their CRF is allocated based on the 
recommendations of the successive Finance Co mmissions. Funds allocated in the CRF are for 
managing the various identified natural calamities and no calami ty-wise allocations in the CRF 
are made by the Finance Commissions. 
 State-wise details of the allocation and releas es of Central Share of Calamity Relief Fund 
(CRF) and assistance released to the States from NCCF for  management of notified calamities 
during the year 2008-09, are given in the statement (See below). 
 As per the scheme of CRF/NCCF, 2005-10,  State Level Committee is responsible to 
ensure that the money drawn from the CRF is actually utilized for the purposes for which the CRF 
has been set up, and only on items of expenditure and as per norms contained in the guidelines 
issued by the Government of India. Scheme also  provides that accounts of the fund shall be 
maintained by the Accountant General in charge of accounts in the State in the normal course. 
Controller and Auditor General of India would caus e audit of CRF to be conducted every year in 
terms of the purposes of the CRF scheme.

 1038. SHRI JAI PARKASH AGGARWAL: Will the Minister of LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
be pleased to state: 
 (a)  whether Government is considering change in labour laws, if so, the details thereof as 
the existing labour laws in the country are a plethora of outdated laws, many of which need to be 
scrapped or changed; 
 (b)  whether Government has amended the Factor ies Act, 1948 during the last five years, if 
so, the details thereof; and 
 (c)  whether there is a proposal to furthe r amend the Factories Act, 1948 and Industrial 
Disputes Act, 1947, if so, the details thereof? 
 THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINI STRY OF LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT  
(SHRI OSCAR FERNANDES): (a) Review/updation of  labour laws is an ongoing process in 
order to bring them in tune with the emergi ng needs of the economy such as increasing 
production, productivity, employment etc. Th e required changes in the labour laws are 
accomplished by the Government after detailed consul tation with the social partners with a view 
to harmonize the interests of all stake holders. 
 (b) No, Sir. 
 (c) The Bill to amend the Section 66 of the Fa ctories Act, 1948 to provide flexibility in the 
matter of employment of women worker during ni ght shift with adequate safeguards has been 
introduced in the Parliament. The proposals to further amend the Factories Act, 1948 and the 
Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 are being formulated.  
Violation of labour laws in Noida 
 1039. SHRI K. CHANDRAN PILLAI: Will the Minister of LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT be 
pleased to state: 
 (a)  whether Government is aware of the incide nt in Noida in which a CEO of an Italian firm 
died; 
 (b)  if so, the details thereof; 
 (c)  whether any enquiry has been conducted into the incident; 
 (d)  whether there were any violation of  labour laws by the company management; 
 (e)  if so, the details thereof; and 
 (f)  the measures proposed to be taken in this regard and the details thereto? 
 THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINI STRY OF LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT  
(SHRI OSCAR FERNANDES): (a) and (b) Yes, Sir.  According to information received from 

 282
Government of Uttar Pradesh, late Shri Lalit Kumar Chaudhary, Chief Executive Officer of  
M/s/ Grazino Transmissioni India Ltd., Greater Noida was beaten to death by agitated and 
locked out workers in the factory on 22.09.2008. 
 (c) Yes, Sir. The FIR was lodged by the Graz ino management in the Bisrakh police station, 
Gautambudh Nagar on the same day and the police investigation is under progress. 
 (d) and (e) Government of Uttar Pradesh has informed that prima facie, violation of any 
labour laws did not come to the notice of administration. The mana gement locked out 218 
workers and the work ers were agitating against this lockout. The management had taken the 
ground that the strike by the workers was illegal. The matter has been referred to the Labour 
Court for adjudication on 04.10.2008 and thus the matter is subjudice. 
 (f) The State Government of Uttar Pradesh has delegated the powers of Labour 
Commissioner to the Chief Executive Officers of  Noida and Greater Noida in their respective 
jurisdiction to ensure better co-ordination and supervision in industrial and labour related matters 
and the officers of the Labour Department operating in the area have been put under the 
administrative control of respective Chief Executive Officers of Noida and Greater Noida. 
 The Chief Executive Officer of Greater Noida has held meetings with the management of 
M/s. Grazino Transmissioni and assured them of  all possible assistance to maintain cordial 
industrial atmosphere. Adequate security has been also been provided around the factory 
premises. 
Non implementation of child labour laws properly 
 †1040. SHRI MOTILAL VORA: 
  SHRI SATYAVRAT CHATURVEDI: 
 Will the Minister of LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT be pleased to state: 
 (a)  whether Government is aware that laws  related to children and child labour are not 
being implemented properly in the country; 
 (b)  if so, which are the States where these laws are not implemented properly; 
 (c)  the initiatives taken by Government in this regard; and 
 (d)  the steps taken by Government to prevent use of children in beggary? 
 THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINI STRY OF LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT  
(SHRI OSCAR FERNANDES): (a) and (b) Implemen tation of law is an ongoing process. 
Section 2 (i) of the Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act,  1986, entrust the powers of 
implementation of the Act to the State Governme nts in establishments other than those under 
the control of the Central Government or a railway  administration or a major port or a mine or 
oilfield. Therefore, the State Governments are sole ly responsible to implement the provisions of 
the Act. 
†Original notice of the question was received in Hindi. 

 283
 (c) The Central Government has constitute d a Central Monitoring Committee to monitor 
implementation of the Child Labour (Prohibition  and Regulation) Act, 1986, and is implementing 
the National Child Labour Project Scheme wherein bridge education alongwith stipend, mid-day 
meal, health check-up are provided to the ch ildren withdrawn from work in the hazardous 
occupations and processes. 
 (d) Begging is not listed in the Schedule to the Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) 
Act, 1986 listing hazardous occupations and processes. However, under the National Charter for 
Children Resolution passed by the Ministry of  Women and Child Development, the Government 
is committed to protect children from all forms of economic exploitation and the prevent their use 
in any illegal activities such as prostitution and begging etc.

security to the workers in th e unorganized sector, many of whom are unemployed. In this 
context, the Government has already introduced a Bill in the Parliament.

Constitution of national land reform council 
 1048. SHRI PYARELAL KHANDELWAL: Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be 
pleased to state: 

 295
 (a)  what is the implication with regard to “National Land Reform Council” and by when it is 
likely to be constituted; 
 (b)  whether it is a fact that lack of land reforms throughout the country amounts to 
dodging the poor people though sixty years have passed since independence;  
 (c)  if so, the action Government is goi ng to take with regard to the above; 
 (d)  whether Government would consider the fa rm Road Poverty alleviation Ministry for rural 
poor population on the lines to urban poverty alleviation Ministry; and 
 (e)  if so, the details thereof? 
 THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINIST RY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT (SHRI CHANDRA 
SEKHAR SAHU): (a) to (c) Land reforms related issues essentially fall in the domain of the 
State Governments. The Central Government has a limited role  to play, being mainly advisory in 
nature. Implementation of land reforms programme s  i s  r e v i e w e d  f r o m  t i m e  t o  t i m e  a t  v a r i o u s  
fora, including Conferences of the Revenue Mini sters/Secretaries of States and UTs organized 
by the Ministry of Rural Development. However, the subject matter has been considered at the 
highest level. In order to get comprehensive recommendations on the matter, it has been

RESOLUTION 
New Delhi, the 9th January, 2008 
Subject: Constitution of the "Committee on State Agrarian Relations and the Unfinished Task 
in Land Reforms". 
 No.21013/4/2007-LRD.—Good governance in land administration and effective 
management of agrarian relations are important catalysts for poverty reduction and economic 
development. Socially just access to land, land-related services and security of land rights are of 
utmost importance in achieving the desired pace and level of economic growth and sustainable 
development.  
 2. Land reforms can change the current cult ure of exclusion so that the poor can gain 
access to land, credit, technology, markets and other productive services, and become active 
partners in the development of government policies and programmes affecting their livelihood.

recording of all agricultural tenants and a fr amework to enable cultivators of land to 
lease in and lease out with suitable assuranc es for fair rent, security of tenure and 
right to resumption. 
 (v) To examine the issues relating to alienation  of tribal Islands including traditional rights 
of the forest-dependant tribals and to su ggest realistic measur es including changes 
required in the relevant laws for restoration of such lands to them. 
 (vi) To examine the issue of setting up of fast track courts/mechanism for speedy 
disposal of land-related litigation cases. 
 (vii) To look into the land use aspects, part icularly the agricultural land, and recommend 
measures to prevent/minimize  conversion of agricultural land for non-agricultural 
purposes, consistent with development needs of the country. 
 (viii) To examine the issues related to ho mestead rights and recommend measures for 
providing land for housing to the families without homestead land. 
 (ix) To suggest measures for modernization of land management with special reference 
to updating of land records, proper recordin g of land rights and speedy resolution of 
conflicts and disputes relating of land. 
 (x) Suggest institutional mechanisms for effective implementation of land reform 
programmes. 
 (xi) To examine measures to provide women greater access to land and other productive 
assets. 
 (xii) Any other issue of relevance. 

 303
 (xiii) Any other Term of Reference that ma y be decided by the Committee in its first 
meeting. 
 5. The Committee may visit the States and ho ld consultations with them in order to 
finalize its recommendations. 
 6. The Committee would make recommendations on the programme of action for 
effective implementation of land reforms with particular reference to the above matters in 
cosultation with State Governments/Union Territory Administrations. 
 7. The Committee may set up sub-groups/task forces, if necessary, for undertaking in-
depth studies on the above components of the Terms of Reference. 
 8. The Committee may co-opt any other official/non-official/experts/representatives of 
other agencies. 
 9. The Committee will submit its final repo rt within one year from the date of its 
constitution and the report will be placed before the National Council for Land Reforms for its 
consideration and directions. 
 10. The expenditure of the official members of the Committee for attending the meetings of 
the Committee will be borne by the respective pa rent Department/Ministry/Organisations as per 
the rules applicable to them.  The expenditure on TA/DA of non-official Members will be borne 
by the Department of Land Resources according to the appropriate rules and practices. 
 11. The Committee will be located in and serviced by the Department of Land Resources in 
the Ministry of Rural Development at New Delhi.

 1053. SHRIMATI JAYA BACHCHAN: Will the Mi nister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased 
to state: 
 (a)  whether it is a fact that as a result of implementation of NREGA East-West corridor, 
the number of migrants from Bihar and Uttar Pradesh has gone down considerably; 
†Original notice of the question was received in Hindi.

 (b)  whether this has affected paddy cultivatio n in States like Punjab which is experiencing 
severe labour crunch and is set to bring down the area under paddy cultivation; and 
 (c)  the steps taken by Government to address the problem? 
 THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINIST RY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT (SHRI CHANDRA 
SEKHAR SAHU): (a) There is no programme by the "NREGA East-West corridor" being 
implemented by the Ministry. However, Government had enacted National Rural Employment 
Guarantee Act, 2005 in September, 2005. The Act provides for a legal guarantee for 100 days of 
wage employment to adult members of every ru ral household in a financial year for doing 
unskilled manual work on demand. The workers are free to avail any other employment 
opportunity available to them in their State or elsewhere. NREGA  has been extended to the rural 
areas in the country in a phased manner. 200 di stricts were covered in the first phase with  
effect from 2.2.2006. 130 additional districts were  covered in the second phase during the year 
2007-08 and all the remaining rural areas have been covered under the Act from 1.4.2008. 
 (b) This Ministry has not received any report  from the Government of Punjab regarding 
paddy cultivation being affected in the State du e to labour crunch on account of launch of 
NREGA.

Denial of wages to women and old workers under NREGS 
 1064. SHRIMATI VIPLOVE THAKUR: Will the Mi nister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased 
to state: 

 324
 (a) whether it has been brought to the notice of Government that the children, women 
and old do not perform much work such as the young people under the scheme of NREGA; 
 (b) if so, the details thereof; 
 (c) whether it is a fact that they are denied of wages because of their low performance 
and sometimes asked for bribe by Panchayat Pradhan for paying their wages;

 THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINIST RY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT (SHRI CHANDRA 
SEKHAR  SAHU): (a) to (d) In accordance with Section 2(a) of the NREG Act, "adult" means 
a person who has completed 18 years of age. Th erefore, Children below 18 year of age are not 
eligible for getting employment under NREG Ac t, 2005. Para 7 of Schedule 1 of NREG Act 
stipulates that when wages are directly linked with  the quantity of work, the wages shall be paid 
according to the schedule of rates fixed by the State Government for different types of work 
every year, in consultation with the State Council. Further, Para 8 of Schedule 1 of NREG Act 
provided that the schedule of rates of wages for unskilled labourers shall be so fixed that a 
person working for seven hours would normally earn a wage equal to the wage rate. Vide 
notification dated 14th January 2008, Para 8 of Schedule 1 has been amended to provide for nine 
hours of work, including one hour of interval of rest against the earlier period of seven hours to 
earn a wage equal to the wage rate. Provision for average out turn of work put out by the 
NREGA workers has also been made in Schedule 1 of the Act by inserting Para 8-A after Para 8 
which reads as under: "The average out-turns of work put out by men and women workers 
working in a group will be the basis for fixing task based Schedule of rates so that there is no 
gender discrimination in the Schedule of rates." 
 The Ministry has not received any report from  the State Governments regarding payment of 
bribe by the workers to the Panchayat Pradhans for getting their wages.

Working hours fixed for NREGA workers 
 1067. SHRIMATI BRINDA KARAT: Will the Minist er of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to 
state: 
 (a) what is the working hours fixed by Government for NREGA workers; 
 (b) whether Government has amended the Schedule to increase the working hours; and 
 (c) if so, the details thereof and the reasons? 
 THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINIST RY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT (SHRI CHANDRA 
SEKHAR  SAHU): (a) to (c) Para 8 of Schedule 1 of NREG Act provided that the Schedule of 
rates of wages for unskilled labourers shall be so fixed that a person working for seven hours 
would normally earn a wage equal to the wage rate. The Government, vide notification dated 
14th January, 2008 has substituted Para 8 of Schedule 1 of National Rural Employment 
Guarantee Act as under: 
 (i) "8(1) The Schedule of rates of wages fo r various unskilled labourers shall be so fixed 
that an adult person working for nine hours would normally earn a wage equal to the 
wage rate. 
  8(2) The working days of an adult worker shall be so arranged that inclusive of 
intervals of rest, if any, it shall not spread over more than twelve hours on any day." 
 (ii) After Para 8, following Para shall be inserted, namely:- 
  "8-A. The average out-turns of work put out by men and women workers working in a 
group will be the basis for fixing task based Schedule of rates so that there is no 
gender discrimination in the Schedule of rates." 
 It has been further clarified vide circular dated 28.5.08 that nine hours of work as indicated 
in para 8(i) above is inclusive of one hour of interval of rest. 

 328
 The above amendment has been carried out to bring NREG Act in conformity with Minimum 
Wages Act, 1984, in so far as the issues of working hours and wage rates are concerned.
